clue.text: Monkeys: small groups of like-minded individuals

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
camps are factions sharing a point of view, as in 'the rival camps'

explanation.surface: A naturalist observes that monkeys form little cliques of kindred spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkeys, as a verb-turned-noun for mischievous children, are rascals or little rogues.

clue.text: "Our Mutual Friend", say, which makes the set?

definitions.text: "Our Mutual Friend", say, which makes the set?

parts.words: "Our Mutual Friend", say, which makes the set?
parts.note: the Dickens novel's title names a friend, and one more book completing a series is a matching partner on the shelf

explanation.surface: Is Dickens's novel the book that completes the collection?
explanation.definitionFit: A book published to accompany or complete another, and the title's mutual friend is literally a companion in book form.

clue.text: Battle ruin given energy, new energy

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin
E is the physics symbol for energy
go means energy or vigour, as in full of go

explanation.surface: Wreckage is revitalised by fresh vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: MARENGO was Napoleon's 1800 victory in northern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of an 1800 battle won by Napoleon over the Austrians, so an example of a battle.

clue.text: This local woven material

indicators.note: woven suggests threads of these words interlaced into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper points out the region's handwoven fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailcloth is strong canvas used for making sails, a kind of material.

clue.text: Top-notch detective capturing hearts

indicators.note: the detective's name holds the other piece within it, as a captor holds a prisoner

parts.note: Albert Campion is the gentleman sleuth of Margery Allingham's novels
H is the card-playing abbreviation for the hearts suit

explanation.surface: A first-rate sleuth wins people over.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, the word means first-class or excellent, a synonym of top-notch.

clue.text: Belittle mass held in NEC complex

indicators.note: the pile is held inside the scrambled letters
complex suggests the letters NEC are tangled up

parts.note: a heap is a mass or pile

explanation.surface: A huge gathering at the NEC complex is played down.
explanation.walkthrough: The NEC is Birmingham's National Exhibition Centre, a big venue for trade fairs.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheapen someone is to lower their worth or dignity, a synonym of belittle.

clue.text: Old poet changing start of The Hunter

indicators.note: the first letter of the hunter's name is changed for another, O becoming A

parts.note: Orion is the hunter of Greek myth, and the constellation named after him

explanation.surface: An ancient bard rewrites the opening of a poem called The Hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: Arion was a semi-legendary Greek lyric poet saved from drowning by a dolphin.

clue.text: Type of make-up, one in fancy pack with lace at the end

indicators.note: the article goes inside the scrambled letters
fancy suggests an elaborate rearrangement of pack

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one

indicators.note: at the end picks the final letter of lace

explanation.surface: A cosmetics kit, elaborately packaged with a lace trim.
explanation.definitionFit: Pancake is a thick, flat stage foundation applied with a damp sponge, a kind of cosmetic.

clue.text: For Annette, worth remaking a picture

indicators.note: a film remake reworks the original, so these letters are reworked too

explanation.surface: For an actress called Annette, it is worth remaking an old film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picture' means a film here: the 1954 Brando drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscar-winning Elia Kazan film, a picture in the movie sense.

clue.text: Without alternative, as time failed to pay off house loan?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the scrambled letters sit around the other piece
the words as time have failed, collapsing into a new order

parts.note: or is the little word that introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Someone with no other option runs out of time and cannot clear their mortgage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside here, not lacking: AMTISE (the anagram of AS TIME, from 'failed') goes around OR.
explanation.definitionFit: To amortise a debt such as a mortgage is to pay it off gradually by instalments; the question mark flags a definition by example.

clue.text: Soldier returning at his time of day to light up

indicators.note: returning makes the soldier's two letters travel back the other way

parts.note: GI is an American private soldier
the American soldier's own spelling of night, as on a diner sign

explanation.surface: A soldier coming home at dusk lights a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' refers back to the GI, so the time of day is spelt the American way, NITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignite something is to set it alight, a direct synonym of light up.

clue.text: Deliver beastly baby Brown

definitions.meaning: as a verb, of a deer: to give birth to a young one

explanation.surface: An instruction to a vet: deliver the animal's brown-coated offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb for a doe giving birth and the name of a pale tan colour.

clue.text: Capital is accessible in change, maybe

indicators.note: the accessible word goes inside the scrambled letters
maybe suggests the word change could be some other arrangement of its letters

parts.note: a shop that is accessible is open

explanation.surface: Money is easy to come by in small coins, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' and 'change' both suggest money, but one is a city and the other is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danish capital city, so a direct example of a capital.

clue.text: Kept lover's ring, see, after performance

indicators.note: the ring and see come after the performance

parts.note: a gig is a musical performance
O is ring-shaped
lo is an old word for see, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: A kept man's ring was seen after a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigolo is a man paid or kept by an older woman as her companion and lover.

clue.text: Chemical weapon — face wind

parts.note: to face up to something takes nerve, and nerve is cheek or boldness
gas is a polite word for flatulence, wind in the stomach

explanation.surface: A soldier must brave a poisonous gust on the battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarin and VX are examples of these toxic agents used in chemical warfare.

clue.text: Proof of saint's transfiguration in balance

indicators.note: the scrambled saint goes inside the remainder word

parts.note: the rest is the balance, what remains

indicators.note: a transfiguration is a change of form, so saint changes into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Evidence of a holy figure's transformation, kept in equilibrium.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof as a suffix, as in waterproof, means able to withstand something, a synonym.

clue.text: Garden flowers: the latest picture

parts.note: snaps is short for snapdragons, the antirrhinums of cottage gardens
hot news or the hot look is the latest

explanation.surface: A garden magazine announces the newest photograph of its flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a quickly taken photograph, a kind of picture.

clue.text: Brad, while on Universal set, ignoring film star group

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces sit on top of the Universal letter

parts.note: a brad is a small thin nail, much like a peg
as can mean while, as in 'as I was leaving'
U is the film classification for universal

indicators.note: ignoring means the film star's letters are left out of set

parts.note: ET is the alien star of Spielberg's film

explanation.surface: Brad Pitt on a Universal film set, ignoring a group of famous actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brad' looks like the actor but is a nail; 'star group' tempts too, but the group is the constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Pegasus is a constellation, a group of stars named after the winged horse.

clue.text: Tense construction worker set off

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
a rigger erects scaffolding or rigging on a building site

explanation.surface: An anxious builder starts work.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger an alarm or a reaction is to set it off.

clue.text: You, having changed just one letter, should get a medal!

indicators.note: one letter of the word for you is swapped for another, here O giving way to I

parts.note: the clue addresses the person solving the puzzle

explanation.surface: A congratulatory note: one small change and you deserve a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You' is the person solving; change the O of that word to I for the second-place medal.
explanation.definitionFit: The second-place award at the Olympics and elsewhere, below gold and above bronze.

clue.text: Musical Holiday (25 March)

definitions.meaning: the nickname of the jazz singer Billie Holiday
the Feast of the Annunciation, a traditional English quarter day

explanation.surface: A show-tune break pencilled in for late March.
explanation.walkthrough: Quarter days are the four dates on which English rents were traditionally due.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the jazz singer's nickname and the name of the Annunciation feast, one of the English quarter days.

clue.text: Hobo's besotted with bling and spirits

indicators.note: besotted means muddled with drink, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Tramps, drunk and infatuated with flashy jewellery, are full of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' teases alcohol after 'besotted'; it means goblins.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobgoblins are mischievous sprites of folklore, so a kind of spirit.

clue.text: Contender who puts Jack in his place?

definitions.text: who puts Jack in his place?
definitions.meaning: jokingly, one who boxes, putting the Jack-in-the-box toy into its case

explanation.surface: A rival who knows how to take Jack down a peg.
explanation.definitionFit: A prizefighter is a contender in the ring, and whimsically one who boxes things up.

clue.text: Lift Democrat offensive

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics
food that is off smells offensive

explanation.surface: A rude American politician gets a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: To doff a hat is to lift it in greeting.

clue.text: Investigate former area of England

parts.note: to suss something out is to investigate it
ex means former, as in ex-wife

explanation.surface: A historian looks into a lost English region.
explanation.walkthrough: SUSSEX is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic county and former Saxon kingdom in southern England, so an example of such an area.

clue.text: Deterrent to one who'd steal a broadsheet setter, possibly not Paisley?

indicators.note: not means the Paisley name is left out of the newspaper

parts.note: the Guardian is a British broadsheet newspaper
Ian Paisley was the Northern Irish politician and preacher
a setter is one kind of dog, hence possibly

explanation.surface: A puzzle compiler for a quality paper, though not Ian Paisley, keeps burglars away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the puzzle compiler (this is the Guardian's own crossword); it is the breed of dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog trained to protect property and scare off burglars deters thieves.

clue.text: A tailor at times rues working in topless coat

indicators.note: the reworked letters go inside the shortened coat word
topless means the coat word loses its first letter

parts.note: to smear is to coat a surface thinly

indicators.note: working means the letters of rues are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A tailor sometimes regrets fitting a coat with no top.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor takes measurements for a fitting, so at times is one who measures; a definition by example.

clue.text: Political supporter drops resistance to a new Far Eastern corporation

indicators.note: drops means the resistance letter falls out of the supporter's word

parts.note: a Tory is a supporter of the UK Conservative Party
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: new signals the letters of to a in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A party loyalist gives up opposing a new company from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' makes TOY from TORY, and 'new' turns TO A into OTA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese carmaker is a large corporation based in the Far East.
